intro.speaker: Kaldor the Kingbreaker
lines: FELIX: Your Majesty, as I promised. Here they are.
So. You're the one Felix keeps talking about.
Look at me. I don't age a day. I was chosen, you see. That's why.
My master put me on this throne five hundred years ago. And then... nothing. Not a word. Not in a very long time.
I've come to think that means I'm trusted. To do what's best for the kingdom. And what's best for the kingdom is war.
Five hundred years I've spent building the most vicious army in all the lands. We start with the wizard kingdom.
But it appears I'll have to deal with you first.

Y: The Throne of a Hundred Challengers: every weapon tagged with its owner's name. The last tag: AUREK THE TALL. Almost.
k: Torches in a full ring, mirrors behind them. Light from every side, so the king casts no shadow.
Some of the mirrors are old-world glass. They don't fog. They don't scratch. They show the room a moment late.
1: The doors, back to the hall.
=: The carpet ends at the foot of the throne, worn through where people have knelt.
I: A black pillar. In its shadow, the shadow is slightly too dark.
f: A portrait of Kaldor, twice life size. The painter has given him a halo. Then thought better of it, and made it a crown.

objects.name: Kaldor
lines: I do not like them. I keep them.

objects.name: King Brannoc
lines: A king. Me. I keep reaching for my sword and finding a sceptre.
Go on ahead, friend. I shall catch you up. Somehow. Kings can do that, I am told.

objects.name: Royal Advisor
lines: His Majesty is working remotely. He has left two rules: don't go to war, and don't cause problems.
I've had them framed. Then I had the frame framed. One can't be too careful.

answer: No war. No problems. Some disagreement about the moat.
His Majesty replies to ravens within three to five business days. Nobody knows what a business day is. We are afraid to ask.

objects.name: Royal Steward
lines: Your Majesty. The throne is warm, the kingdom is confused, and there's a queue.
You'll be working remotely, I take it? Everyone's doing it. Two rules while you're out: no wars, no problems. I'll hold the fort. Literally.
